summary: No fundamentals thesis is broken by evidence in close.json. The only fill today was a small MSM buy ($8, 9/9 F-score, cfo $306M vs net income $223M), and its thesis was written today. Every held single-stock position is within about 3% of cost (DPZ -1.4%, CARG -1.4%, FAST -0.7%, MSCI -0.6%, IDXX +1.0%, KR +2.1%, VRSN +2.8%, WMT +0.9%). The largest daily drops (MSCI -2.6%, FAST -1.8%, VRSN -1.7%, IDXX -1.6%) came with a tech and communication rotation, and none comes with a filing, guidance cut, restatement or cfo-below-net-income finding. None is near its stated stop. Lesson L1 and L2 name the proposer, news-analyst and portfolio-manager, not me, so neither changed my calls. I only note that L1's unfixed DPZ stop still applies. The 5-session BTC/USD loss (-5.0% graded wrong) is a trend call, not a fundamentals call.
update: Watch items, none of them a break. (1) DPZ: the $274.88 invalidation is still anchored to the $305.42 reference close, not the $316.58 fill (about 13% below fill, per L1), and the position is -1.4%. The PM should re-anchor it. Its fundamentals check (cfo above net income, still on the screen) needs the next fundamentals menu, since close.json has no new data on it. (2) IDXX: earnings are estimated for 11-02, and the thesis requires cfo above net income and no underperformance versus XLV greater than 5 points over 21 days. Re-test it against the post-print filing, not the current -1.6% day. (3) MSM: the filings it rests on predate today's fill, so a new 8-K or guidance change is the only thing that should break it. Its current -0.3% is noise. (4) CARG, KR, WMT and DPZ have earnings or guidance catalysts that are all outside the next few sessions (CARG 11-05, WMT 11-19, KR 12-03), so there is no fundamental reason to act before then. Shadow portfolio is ahead of the agent (+4.9% vs +0.1%), but that gap comes from names we did not hold, such as RRC (deal-driven), and is not evidence against any held thesis.
